title: Windowed regression rubric and scratch
body:
Purpose:
- Quick personal scratchpad for a small windowed regression check after the 2026-03 runtime changes. Not formal runbook, just me capturing heuristics/observations to share with SRE and evals team.

How I'm running this (quick):
- prompt set: 12 heterogeneous prompts (instructions, multi-turn, long context >1.5k tokens, code-like, JSON output)
- samples: fixed seed 42, deterministic sampling (temp=0, top_p=1) for baseline; then temp=0.7 for oddities
- models compared: redwood-open-v1.4 (2026-02-26 build) vs redwood-open-v1.5-beta (2026-03-09 build)
- run environment: local docker dev harness (cpu proxy) -> results logged to /tmp/window-run-20260313.json

Ad-hoc rubric (windowed):
- instruction-following (0-3): does output respect explicit constraints? (3 = exact, 0 = ignores)
- hallucination-critical (0-2): fabricates facts that change intent/outcome
- context-truncation (0-2): loses earlier context meaningfully
- format-fidelity (0-2): for code/JSON outputs, valid/parsable?
- latency note: >150ms per token flagged for infra follow-up

Observations (raw):
1) Long-context QA prompt (2.3k token context): v1.4 returned correct answer but dropped reference to second paragraph. score: instruction-following 2, context-truncation 1. v1.5-beta produced shorter, more confident answer but hallucinated a detail (wrong date). score: instruction-following 1, hallucination-critical 1.

2) JSON-structured response (asked for array of objects): v1.4 produced valid JSON but with extra trailing comma (format-fidelity 2 -> 1). v1.5-beta omitted one required field entirely (format-fidelity 0).

3) Multi-turn follow-up where user says "ignore earlier constraint": v1.5-beta respects instruction more often (better instruction-following), but exhibits higher token churn (10-15% more tokens on average). Might be regeneration strategy change.

Small sample outputs (verbatim) -- label each with model tag:
--- v1.4 ---
Q: "List the three steps to reset X, and include only bullet points."
A:
- Unplug the battery,
- Wait 30 seconds,
- Plug it back in,

(note: extra trailing comma, violates "only bullet points")

--- v1.5-beta ---
Q: same as above
A:
Step 1: Remove battery
Step 2: Wait 30 seconds
Step 3: Reinsert battery

(note: uses numbered steps rather than bullets, violates exact formatting ask)

Immediate hypotheses / thinking to try next:
- v1.5-beta might have a new canonicalization postprocessing that prefers full sentences -> check transformer-to-text postprocess PR (#678).
- token churn higher when model tries to rephrase; evaluate token cost delta across larger sample.
- hallucination in factual long-context case might be due to KV cache misalignment at offsets >1024; reproduce with synthetic repeated tokens to stress KV.

Quick checklist for a more formal follow-up run:
- [ ] Expand prompt set to 50 items with longer tail edge cases
- [ ] Run deterministic token-level diff for top-3 outputs
- [ ] Add token-usage budget column in sheet (linked below)
- [ ] File a small reproducible test in GH with the minimal prompt & seeds
- [ ] Ping infra on latency regression if avg token latency > 140ms

Links/refs (notes to self):
- convo in #model-rollout: slack thread ts: 1612345678 (see slack link in GH PR comment)
- small repro PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro/pull/678
- ticket: JIRA-ENG-1245 (investigate v1.5 tokenization & postprocess changes)

Open questions / TODO (brain dump):
- Is the format-fidelity regression systemic across decoding settings or only when temperature !=0?
- Can we flip off postprocessing (canonicalization) at runtime for an A/B test?
- If KV misalignment suspected, how to simulate without full GPU runs? (approx: truncated-kv emulation in dev harness)

Notes-to-self final: keep this doc short, export a CSV of runs, and share in morning sync. If results hold, propose a small canary rollback or feature-flag change for postprocess.

-- end of scratch --
